Plots each control unit's weight and its own estimate

Source: R/plot.R
sdid_units_plot.Rd

Synthetic difference-in-differences estimates the effect as a weighted average, over the control units, of the difference-in-differences comparison of the treated units with each control alone, using the time weights. This plot shows those comparisons with their unit weights, for an estimate or each cohort of a staggered design.

Usage

sdid_units_plot(
  estimates,
  type = c("scatter", "bars"),
  cohort = NULL,
  label.units = NULL,
  weighted.only = FALSE
)

Arguments

estimates

The result of sdid(), or a named list of results with a single adoption period each, drawn in panels labeled by their names. A staggered result is drawn with a panel for each cohort, unless cohort chooses one.

type

The kind of plot. "scatter" (the default) plots each control's weight against its own estimate. "bars" draws a bar from the effect to each weighted control's own estimate, ordered by weight. See Details.

cohort

For a staggered result, the adoption period of the one cohort to plot, as it appears in the result's cohorts. Defaults to NULL, plotting every cohort in its own panel.

label.units

Which controls to name. "all" names every control, "weighted" those with positive weight, and a whole number n the n with the largest weights, with any tied at the cutoff included. Defaults to "all" for a single panel and 10 for several. The scatter still draws the controls it leaves unnamed, while the bars draw only the controls they name.

weighted.only

TRUE to leave controls with no weight out of the scatter. Defaults to FALSE, drawing them as open circles.

Value

A ggplot object, which draws the plot when printed and can be extended with +, for example with labels, themes or further layers. Scales, facets and coordinate systems added this way replace those the plot sets.

Details

type = "scatter" (the default) plots each control's weight against its own estimate, with the effect as a red line, so that the controls that make up the synthetic control are at the right and whether they agree with each other is seen in their spread about the line. Every control is drawn, those with no weight as open circles, so that the plot also shows whether the weighting changed the answer, and label.units chooses which are named. type = "bars" draws a bar for each control with weight chosen by label.units, ordered from the largest weight down, running from the effect to the control's own estimate, with its weight at the end. A control pulls the estimate up if its bar runs right of the line and down if left, by its weight times the bar's length.

Requires ggplot2, and the ggrepel package to place the scatter's labels without overlap. Without ggrepel, labels that would overlap are left out.
